records.c: Reads the stage metadata following $FCC0. Sets the stage palette and initial vertical view, loads the tile and attribute grid pointers and dimensions, prepares row pointers and calculates scroll limits.

Fills four split tables at $0856, $0876, $0896 and $08B6 with the tile and attribute addresses of 32 rows, adding the stage width each time. Then computes horizontal and vertical bounds in character-cell units.
Divides the 16-bit horizontal and 8-bit vertical character coordinates by four. Adds the resulting column to the selected tile-row address and returns that 4 by 4 tile ID.

Builds a 40-column view from the selected starting position. For each character position it finds the containing tile, selects one of sixteen indices in that tile and fetches its VIC colour from $CF00 before writing both screen buffers.

Writes the character code in A to the same row and column of the $4800 and $4C00 screen buffers and writes the colour from $05 to colour RAM. The routine patches its own immediate operand to save the character while computing the destination pointers.
Eight masks select one active-low CIA1 port A output per scan, in the order $FE,$FC,$FB,$F7,$EF,$DF,$BF,$7F. The second sample selects two columns.
Eight CIA1 port B samples written in scan order by the keyboard routine at $18D7. A low bit reports a closed switch in a selected column.
Sets CIA1 A to output and B to input, then applies the eight masks from $18C6 and saves the port B samples at $18CE. The saved X and Y are restored from immediate operands patched on entry.
Masks interrupts, maps RAM over BASIC and the KERNAL, initializes the active mission to 1 and calls the mission disk loader before configuring the display.
Turns off the display, selects VIC bank $4000 through CIA2 and caches the bank select with two values for the serial clock line. Stops the CIA2 timers before initial screen construction.
Starts a new player setup, clears score state and saves the current mission for both players. Sets the starting counters using the selected one-player or two-player mode.
Checks whether the active player has lives and whether their stored mission matches the loaded one, before dispatching to the appropriate setup path.

Reads the active player's stage index, selects the alternate graphics when it matches $FCF5, constructs the stage's lookup tables, applies object placements and patches the call at $1AB3 to the mission setup hook.
Each pass uses this mask to keep selected pixels in one row of every character in the playfield font. A reverse pass uses its inverse to clear those pixels.
Selects the pixel row (0 to 7) to update on each masked pass through the 256 characters.

Runs 32 masked passes across all 256 characters at $4000, each pass touching one row in each glyph. A=0 masks existing destination pixels away. A nonzero takes pixels from $D000, $D800 or $CB00 RAM, selected by $1902 and $ADF7.
Places the RAM handler $1E87 in the hardware IRQ vector, sets the first VIC raster compare to $F8, clears pending sources and enables VIC raster IRQs.

Saves A, acknowledges CIA1 and VIC status, and processes the VIC source bits selected by $28. For a selected source it saves X/Y, reads the raster schedule and replaces the destination of the jump at $1EB6 using the two handler tables.
Advances the raster schedule index. A scheduled line of $FF restarts the schedule at line $21CE. Writes the compare register and restores the saved registers before RTI.
Low bytes of handler addresses. The dispatcher indexes with the handler number from the raster schedule and patches the low JMP operand at $1EB7.
High bytes of handler addresses copied into the JMP operand at $1EB8.
Low eight bits of the first raster compare after the dispatcher restarts the schedule.
Indexed low raster compare values for the dispatcher's return. $FF resets the schedule index and uses the value at $21CE instead.
Handler-table indices parallel to the raster line schedule. Each selected index is copied to $1E86 before dispatch.
Packed decimal seconds. The countdown reloads $59 and borrows from the minute byte when seconds pass below zero.
Packed decimal minutes for the play timer, initialized to 3 by stage entry.
Countdown initialized to $32. Each call of the clock decrements it and the seconds update reloads it at zero.

Counts down from 50 calls, then subtracts one BCD second using decimal mode. Borrows a minute on seconds underflow, and when there are no minutes to borrow sets the timeout outcome and clamps the display to zero.
Places the minutes, colon and two BCD second digits in the panel starting at $53BB. Each digit uses the second numeral set at glyph $14 plus the digit.
Blanks the display and waits on the raster. On first entry installs $284F as the NMI vector, programs both CIA2 timer latches with $4CC7 and starts timer A at the selected raster position.
Writes zero to both CIA2 timer controls and the interrupt control register, then clears the setup flag at $2771.
Mirrors 21 rows of three bytes in the sprite work area at $5400 plus Y. Swaps the outer bytes of each row and reverses their two-bit pixel pairs through the table at $0600.
Copies the 40-character rows of the front screen at $4800 into the alternate $4C00 screen, moving each copied row up one row.
Copies 40-character rows from the $4C00 screen into the $4800 screen with a one-row vertical displacement.
Scans the keyboard, reads joystick port 2 through CIA1 port A and applies seven keyboard masks to the saved control byte. A pressed control clears its corresponding bit in $0ADB.

Rescans the keyboard after the raster line wait. While the colour key is active and the raster tick passes the mask test, increments the active player's colour and updates the first two sprite colours.
Keeps the latest raw masked input in $0ADC. Suppresses player input during the lockout at $0C4D, or sends the input to the demonstration or capture path depending on $9011.
In mode 2 stores a duration and new control byte when the byte changes, then advances the write index and resets the duration.
In mode 1 loads an input byte and its duration whenever the previous duration expires. Decrements the duration and applies the saved byte at $0ADB. A zero byte sets $2C to 1 instead.
Twelve-byte DOS stream name for drive 8. The digit at $3E45 is replaced from the mission index before opening the file, and the suffix requests a PRG stream for reading.
Resets the KERNAL vectors and initializes I/O, sets the twelve-byte filename at $3E3E, opens logical file 1 on drive 8 with secondary address 3 and selects it for input.

Blanks the screen and disables the current raster and CIA interrupt sources, sets the ASCII digit in the mission filename and opens the disk stream. Reads $0500 bytes to $6400 and $3EF0 bytes to $C000, then closes the stream and restores the saved processor port.
Banks in the KERNAL to close the channel after both transfers. The immediate operand at $3F2B holds the processor port saved before the load.

Reads one byte through KERNAL CHRIN, banks out I/O and ROM for the store through $FA/$FB, increments that destination and decrements the remaining length in $FC/$FD. Returns when the counter reaches zero.
Closes logical file 1, clears the channel selections and waits for 255 passages of raster line $F8 before returning. Restores X from the patched operand at $3FA4.
Enumerates all 256 byte values, reverses the order of their four 2-bit fields and stores the result at $0600,X. The table permits horizontal reversal of multicolour pixels.
Clears page $0400 and then seeds $04A0 with $FF.
Ten 8-byte glyphs for digits 0 to 9 in the custom font, each byte holding the eight pixels of one row.
Custom fixed-width glyphs from blank at index $20 through Z at index $3A, eight bytes per character.

Multicolour sprite rows for small flying objects and effects, including the pointed projectiles and round flash shapes. Each 64-byte slot holds 21 three-byte rows followed by one byte outside the displayed height.

Multicolour figure poses and component shapes. Upper bodies, leg silhouettes and horizontally paired poses are stored in consecutive 64-byte slots. The mission loader can replace the slots at $6400-$68FF.
Sixteen sprite slots including compact action poses, swinging limb shapes around $5E80 and paired left/right upper-body poses near $5FC0-$6100.
Sixteen sprite slots around the walking and turning poses. Upper- and lower-body shapes are stored in separate frames.
Figure components with long vertical leg silhouettes and mirrored upper body shapes. The first part is in the region the mission loader overwrites.
Upper-body sprites facing either way and long single-leg poses, followed by crouched figures and horizontally extended pieces.
Tail of the actor-frame block, including compact crouching poses and the tall shapes at $6E00 and $6E40.
Sprite rows for figures facing and moving in both directions, including poses with the legs extended and crouching figures.
Standing figures and extended limbs, paired by facing direction across the block.
Last three sprite slots before the larger effect block. These hold mirrored figure fragments.
Sprite slots containing wide silhouettes and bright effect frames, including repeated horizontal pieces and circular bursts.
Upper and lower pieces of large sprite-drawn objects. The last quarter includes numbered award panels.
Stored 64-byte multicolour frames beyond the live VIC bank. They include repeated figure outlines with altered limbs and matched left and right poses.
Left-facing source frames with poses corresponding to the right-facing art from $8000.
Final resident source shapes beyond the active VIC bank. They include a figure with an extended weapon and large head and body parts.

Selects the active stage's attribute grid and reduces its cells to the low three bits. Applies three-byte records from the active player's half of page $0200. Each gives a destination pointer and a value, and a zero value ends the list. Counts records whose shifted type equals 1, 5, 9, 13 or 14.
Copies 128 bytes from the stage pointer at $FCE9/$FCED into the first or second half of page $0200, selected by the player workspace index.
Fills 200 panel cells at $5320 with the blank glyph and sets the eight sprite pointers at $53F8 to $55.

Clears the text sprite buffer starting at $5400. Walks a zero-ended ASCII message after its leading position byte, converts digits and capitals to glyphs from $5000 and writes eight glyph rows three bytes apart in sprite storage. A digit 1 in these templates uses the active player number at $39.
Sixteen split pointers selected by message number in A. Low bytes are at $9702 and high bytes at $9712. Both indices 4 and 5 select the mission-retention prompt.
Player-number and game-over text. Starts with position byte $74 and ends at the zero before the ready message.
The ready announcement begins with position byte $7C and includes the player-number placeholder.
Tells the player to wait for a new mission. The position byte is $46.
Announces that time ran out. Its template begins at position $74.
Asks the player whether to keep mission 1. Both corresponding pointer-table entries use these same bytes.
Two-line completion message placed by position byte $50.
Two-line objective text placed by position byte $5A.
Title word with position byte $84.
Bonus heading placed by position byte $50.
Two-line practice or demonstration prompt with position byte $46.
Two-line fire prompt with position byte $46 for the sprite renderer.
Perfect result text with position byte $46.
Stage completion text with position byte $64.
Two-line disk loading text with a mission-number slot.
Standalone message selected by index 15 in the sprite message table.
Sixteen VIC colour values selected by bits 2 to 5 of the message delay counter, copied to the first five sprite colours.
Uses A to select a message pointer from $9702/$9712, sets the message state and calls the sprite renderer.

Waits for the $2B flag and clears it on each pass. Cycles the first five sprite colours and allows controls to dismiss the message after the delay counter drops below $5A. Clears sprite enables, expansion and message state on exit.

For the demonstration or the active attract prompt, converts capitals by subtracting $20 and places the fire and player-count text at $5352/$53A3. Active-low right selects mode 3, left selects mode 2 and fire enters the player setup at $19B5.
Two zero-terminated strings for the attract prompt. Mode 3 starts 16 bytes into this table for the two-player message.
Zero-terminated fire prompt for the character screen at $5352, separate from the positioned sprite-message template.

Clears $27E1 and $26, advances the mission number and loads the next file. Restores VIC bank settings, clears colour RAM and waits for fire before clearing sprite enables and reinitializing the next scene.
Ten sequences of sixteen high frequency bytes. The effect updater uses the effect number times sixteen plus the current step and copies the result into the selected voice's high frequency register.
Indexed waveforms and gate control values for a newly selected sound effect.
Indexed attack and decay values applied to the selected voice at its effect start.
Three indices into the active effect's 16-step sequence. A value of $10 means the voice's sequence has finished.
Register offsets 0, 7 and 14 for the SID's three voice register groups.
The effect number currently assigned to each of the three SID voices.

Cycles through the three voice indices and saves A as the chosen voice's effect number. Clears the previous gate, initializes both frequency bytes from the low five bits of VIC control 1 and writes the effect's envelope and waveform.
Visits all three voices and skips a voice whose step is $10. Otherwise advances the step and replaces the voice's frequency high byte from the sixteen-entry sequence selected by its effect number.
